title: Normalization quotient is supported at singular points
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and $X$ a reduced finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] all of whose irreducible components have dimension one [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $
u:X^
u	o X$ be its componentwise normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization], and let $S$ be the set of points at which $X	o\operatorname{Spec}k$ is not smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Then $S$ is a finite set of closed points, each with residue field $k$ via the structural map, $
u$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and there is a short exact sequence of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent]
$$0\longrightarrow\mathcal O_X\longrightarrow
u_*\mathcal O_{X^
u}\longrightarrow Q\longrightarrow0,$$
where $Q\cong igoplus_{x\in S}\mathscr S_x(M_x)$. Here $A_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $C_x=(
u_*\mathcal O_{X^
u})_x$ is the integral closure [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] of $A_x$ in its total ring of fractions (the localization obtained by inverting all non-zero-divisors), $M_x=C_x/A_x$ is a nonzero finite-length $A_x$-module (it admits a finite filtration with simple successive quotients), and $\mathscr S_x(M_x)(U)=M_x$ if $x\in U$, and $0$ otherwise, with $\mathcal O_X(U)$ acting by germs in $A_x$. Writing $\mathfrak m_x$ for the maximal ideal of $A_x$, the completions [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]
$$\widehat A_x=\varprojlim_n A_x/\mathfrak m_x^n,\qquad \widehat C_x=\varprojlim_n C_x/\mathfrak m_x^nC_x$$
have the following properties: $\widehat C_x$ is the integral closure of $\widehat A_x$ in its total ring of fractions, and the natural map induces an $A_x$-linear isomorphism $M_x\cong\widehat C_x/\widehat A_x$.

source.place: Tag 0C1R (lemma-prepare-delta-invariant), parts (1)--(4), (7), (9), specialized to reduced finite-type curves over an algebraically closed field; finite singular support follows from Noetherian quasi-compactness. Smooth and regular loci agree over this perfect field.

proof.text: If $X$ is empty use $S=\varnothing$ and $Q=0$. Otherwise apply the affine/stalk normalization lemma. It gives finite $\nu$, Noetherian local rings, and the structural inclusions $A_x\hookrightarrow C_x$ identifying $C_x$ with the finite integral closure in $Q(A_x)$. The affine and stalk models refer to precisely the componentwise normalization in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0C3B (lemma-stalk-normalization), Tag 0CDV (lemma-normalization-in-terms-of-components); varieties.tex Tag 0BXR (lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic), specialized to reduced finite-type schemes over a field.

proof.text: Apply the coherent-support lemma to $X$. Its canonical cokernel $Q$ gives the displayed coherent short exact sequence and $Q_x=C_x/A_x$. Its equality of normal and smooth loci gives $\operatorname{Supp}Q=S$, a finite set of closed points, with structural residue fields $k$. Every such local ring has dimension one and is essentially of finite type over $k$.

source.place: Tag 0C1R (lemma-prepare-delta-invariant), parts (1)--(3) and proof of the singular support assertion; the smooth-locus identification is Tag 0B8X over the perfect field k.

proof.text: Apply the finite-support coherent-module lemma to this $Q$ on the Noetherian scheme $X$, with support $S$. It gives the canonical germ-map decomposition $Q\cong\bigoplus_{x\in S}\mathscr S_x(Q_x)$ with exactly the stated section values and scalar action. Set $M_x=Q_x=C_x/A_x$; the same lemma gives nonzero finite length and a simple filtration.

source.place: Tag 0C1R (lemma-prepare-delta-invariant), proof of parts (2) and (4): finite closed-support sheaf argument, in its general coherent-module form; sheaves.tex Tag 009C (lemma-stalk-skyscraper-adjoint); algebra.tex Tag 00L5 (lemma-support-point).

proof.text: Fix $x\in S$. Apply the finite-colength completion comparison to $A_x\hookrightarrow C_x$, using finiteness and the simple filtration just obtained. It gives the natural $A_x$-linear isomorphism $M_x\to\widehat C_x/\widehat A_x$ and the canonical algebra isomorphism $C_x\otimes_{A_x}\widehat A_x\cong\widehat C_x$. The curve-normalization/completion lemma applies since $A_x$ is reduced, local, essentially of finite type over $k$, and of dimension one, and $C_x$ is its integral closure. It identifies this tensor algebra with the integral closure of $\widehat A_x$ in $Q(\widehat A_x)$. The latter map sends $b\otimes a$ to $a\phi(b)$, where $\phi$ preserves the denominators from $A_x$; on $1\otimes a$ it is the structural image of $a$. The completion comparison sends this same tensor to $\widehat f(a)\iota_C(1)=\widehat f(a)$. Thus the two algebra identifications preserve the same inclusion of $\widehat A_x$, and their composition gives the asserted completed integral closure.

source.place: Tag 0C1R (lemma-prepare-delta-invariant), parts (7) and (9), finite-module completion and finite-length quotient arguments in the proof; algebra.tex lemma-completion-tensor and lemma-completion-flat give the general finite-module completion inputs.

(1) affine-stalk-closure: R is reduced Noetherian, so Q(R) is the product of the K_i over its minimal primes. T is finite over R, so it is the integral closure of R in Q(R). Localizing at p keeps only the K_i with p_i in p, and integral closure commutes with localization. (2) coherent-support: Q_x=0 exactly when A_x is a normal domain, since a local ring has no nontrivial idempotents. Normal equals regular in dimension at most 1, and regular equals smooth over the perfect k. Purity gives dim A_x=1 and kappa(x)=k at closed points. (3) skyscrapers: a proper generization of a closed point is not closed, so the stalk is supported at the maximal ideal and has finite length by 00L5. The germ maps give a stalkwise isomorphism to the sum of skyscrapers; S empty gives F=0. (4) completion: m^r M=0 and the tower is constant. Completion is exact on finite modules, so M is naturally Ĉ/Â, and Â⊗C is Ĉ as Â-algebras; r=0 is allowed. Parent: step 4 supplies every hypothesis of curve-normalization-completion, and both identifications send 1⊗a to the structural image of a.
